content: The TCT 2014 schedule outlines a series of interviews and discussions with leading medical professionals, focusing on cutting-edge research and clinical trials in the field of interventional cardiology. Saturday, September 13, 2014 At 12:00 PM, Dr. Gary Mintz will be interviewed. The topic of discussion will be his role as a TCT Program Director, with the specific subject to be determined. At 2:00 PM, Dr. The embargo on this study lifts at 12:30 PM on the same day. At 2:30 PM, Dr. George Dangas will participate in a TCT Program Director interview, with the topic yet to be finalized. At 3:30 PM, Dr. Shao Liang Chen will discuss the DKCRUSH-VI trial, which compares FFR-guided versus angiography-guided provisional T-stenting in patients with true coronary bifurcation lesions. The embargo for this study lifts on Sunday, September 14, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Juan Granada will be interviewed as a TCT Program Director, with the topic to be determined. At 4:30 PM, Dr. Steven Yakubov will present the two-year results of the CoreValve US Pivotal Trial, which evaluated a self-expanding bioprosthesis in extremely high-risk patients with aortic stenosis. The embargo lifts at 12:30 PM on September 13, 2014. At 5:00 PM, Dr. William Gray will participate in a TCT Program Director interview, with the topic to be determined. At 5:30 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will provide a daily wrap-up of the TCT events. Sunday, September 14, 2014 At 9:15 AM, Dr. E. Magnus Ohman and Dr. Germano Di Sciascio will engage in a TCT Crossfire debate on whether adequate pretreatment with P2Y12 antagonists is beneficial before PCI in most settings. The embargo lifts at 3:38 PM on the same day. At 9:30 AM, Professor Freek Verheugt will provide a wrap-up of TCT from the Netherlands' perspective. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Roxana Mehran will be interviewed as a TCT Program Director, with the topic to be determined. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Antonio Colombo will present the SECURITY trial, which compares six months versus 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy following coronary drug-eluting stent implantation. The embargo lifts on Monday, September 15, 2014, at 12:06 PM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Matthew Reynolds will discuss the cost-effectiveness analysis of the US CoreValve High Risk Trial, comparing transcatheter aortic valve replacement with a self-expanding device to surgical aortic valve replacement in high-risk patients with aortic stenosis. The embargo lifts on September 13, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 2:00 PM, Professor Colin Berry will present findings from the British Heart Foundation study on fractional flow reserve versus angiography in guiding management to optimize outcomes in non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Yangsoo Jang will discuss the IVUS-CTO trial, which compares intravascular ultrasound-guided versus angiography-guided drug-eluting stent intervention in coronary chronic total occlusions. The embargo lifts at 12:30 PM on the same day. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Rino Sardella will present the SMILE trial, which compares one-stage versus multistage revascularization in multivessel NSTEMI patients. The embargo lifts at 1:00 PM on the same day. At 3:30 PM, Dr. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 16, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Pavel Cervinka will present the OCT STEMI trial, which evaluates optical coherence tomography guidance during primary PCI in acute myocardial infarction. The embargo lifts at 12:30 PM on the same day. At 4:45 PM, Dr. Fausto Feres and Dr. Laura Mauri will debate in a TCT Crossfire session on whether three-month dual antiplatelet therapy is sufficient with drug-eluting stents. At 5:30 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will provide a daily wrap-up of the TCT events. Monday, September 15, 2014 At 9:15 AM, Dr. Keith Oldroyd and Dr. Ran Kornowski will debate in a TCT Crossfire session on whether nonculprit lesion treatment in STEMI is warranted. At 9:30 AM, Dr. Steffen Desch will present the Symplicity Flex trial, a randomized, sham-controlled study of renal sympathetic denervation in patients with refractory hypertension. The embargo lifts on Tuesday, September 16, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 10:00 AM, Dr. Paul Teirstein will discuss the Maintenance of Certification Program. At 10:30 AM, Dr. Samir Kapadia will present five-year results from the PARTNER I trial, which evaluated transcatheter aortic valve replacement with a balloon-expandable device versus conservative care in extremely high-risk patients with aortic stenosis. The embargo lifts on September 13, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Eric Dippel will discuss the EXCITE ISR trial, which compares excimer laser atherectomy to balloon angioplasty for treating femoropopliteal in-stent restenosis. The embargo lifts on September 16, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 11:30 AM, Dr. Fernando Alfonso will present the RIBS IV trial, which compares paclitaxel-eluting balloons to everolimus-eluting stents in patients with coronary in-stent restenosis of drug-eluting stents. The embargo lifts on September 14, 2014, at 12:00 PM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Juan Gaspar will provide a wrap-up in Spanish. At 1:30 PM, Dr. Jeffrey Popma will discuss the past, present, and future of CoreValve. At 2:00 PM, Dr. Rogerio Sarmento-Leite and Dr. Alexandre Quadros will provide a TCT wrap-up in Portuguese. At 3:00 PM, Dr. Tracy Wang will present findings from the TRANSLATE-ACS registry, which compares patterns of use and one-year outcomes with prasugrel versus clopidogrel in patients with acute myocardial infarction undergoing PCI. The embargo lifts on September 15, 2014, at 12:36 PM. At 5:00 PM, Dr. Robert Harrington and Dr. William O'Neill will debate in a TCT Crossfire session on the ethics and generalizability of postprocedure consent in STEMI trials. At 5:15 PM, Dr. Goran Olivecrona and Dr. Vladmir Dzavik will debate in a TCT Crossfire session on the utility of routine aspiration in current practice. At 5:30 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane will provide a daily wrap-up of the TCT events. Tuesday, September 16, 2014 At 9:00 AM, Dr. Philippe Généreux will provide a wrap-up in French. At 9:30 AM, Dr. Robert Byrne and Dr. Rod Stables will provide a wrap-up from the perspective of the UK and Ireland. At 10:15 AM, Dr. Nicolo Piazza and Dr. Michael J. Mack will debate in a TCT Crossfire session on whether TAVR clinical indications should expand to include lower-risk patients. At 11:00 AM, Dr. Jack Lewin will discuss healthcare reform. At 11:30 AM, Dr. Nikolaus Sarafoff will present the ISAR-TRIPLE trial, which compares six weeks versus six months of clopidogrel in patients treated with aspirin and oral anticoagulant therapy following coronary drug-eluting stent implantation. The embargo lifts on September 15, 2014, at 12:06 PM. At 12:00 PM, Dr. Rino Sardella will provide a wrap-up in Italian. At 2:30 PM, Dr. Gregg Stone will present the VELOCITY trial, which evaluates peritoneal hypothermia in patients with acute STEMI undergoing PCI. The embargo lifts on September 15, 2014, at 12:36 PM. At 4:00 PM, Dr. Giora Weisz will provide a wrap-up in Hebrew. At 4:30 PM, Professor Dr. Sigmund Silber will provide a wrap-up in German. At 5:30 PM, Dr. Ajay Kirtane and Dr. Roxana Mehran will provide the final daily wrap-up of the TCT events.
